blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: CXCR4-dependent leukocyte trafficking and marrow retention in WHIM syndrome

item.vignette: A 14-year-old boy has had recurrent bacterial sinusitis and pneumonia since early childhood and has numerous refractory periungual warts. His absolute neutrophil count is 300/mm³, and serum IgG is decreased. Bone marrow examination shows granulocytic hyperplasia with abundant mature neutrophils, many with hypersegmented nuclei and cytoplasmic vacuoles. Genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic variant in CXCR4.
item.lead_in: Which molecular effect most directly explains this patient's neutropenia?

options.A: Failure of B-cell maturation due to absent Bruton tyrosine kinase signaling
options.B: Excess CXCL12-dependent retention of mature leukocytes in the bone marrow due to hyperactive CXCR4 signaling
options.C: Failure of the respiratory burst because of defective phagocyte NADPH oxidase
options.D: Impaired immunoglobulin class switching because of absent CD40 ligand signaling
options.E: Defective actin remodeling in hematopoietic cells due to loss of WASp

item.tested_construct: WHIM syndrome results from gain-of-function CXCR4 signaling with impaired receptor downregulation, causing CXCL12-mediated marrow retention (myelokathexis) and peripheral neutropenia.

explanation.key_explanation: The combination of neutropenia, hypogammaglobulinemia, refractory HPV warts, and a marrow rich in mature neutrophils is WHIM syndrome. Gain-of-function CXCR4 variants impair normal receptor downregulation and prolong CXCL12 signaling, retaining mature leukocytes in marrow rather than allowing normal egress.

distractor_explanations.A: BTK deficiency causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia with failed B-cell maturation, not myelokathexis with mature neutrophil retention.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. Hyperactive CXCR4-CXCL12 signaling causes abnormal retention of mature leukocytes in marrow and peripheral cytopenias.
distractor_explanations.C: Chronic granulomatous disease impairs intracellular killing by phagocytes but does not cause a marrow-retention neutropenia phenotype.
distractor_explanations.D: CD40-ligand deficiency causes a class-switch defect with hyper-IgM physiology, not a marrow packed with retained mature neutrophils.
distractor_explanations.E: WASp deficiency causes eczema, infections, and microthrombocytopenia rather than CXCR4-dependent myelokathexis.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize that WHIM syndrome is a leukocyte-trafficking disorder in which gain-of-function CXCR4 signaling causes CXCL12-mediated marrow retention of mature leukocytes and peripheral neutropenia.

evidence_map.claim: BTK deficiency causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia with failed B-cell maturation, not myelokathexis with mature neutrophil retention.

item.vignette: A 23-year-old woman is hospitalized with disseminated Mycobacterium avium complex infection. item.tested_construct: GATA2 deficiency (MonoMAC/DCML spectrum) is recognized by invasive nontuberculous mycobacterial disease, HPV susceptibility, monocytopenia with B/NK-cell deficiency, and myelodysplasia/myeloid-malignancy predisposition.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Recognition of DADA2 as childhood PAN-like vasculitis with stroke

item.vignette: An 8-year-old boy has recurrent episodes of fever, myalgias, and a violaceous netlike rash on his legs. He has systemic hypertension and has had two small lacunar ischemic strokes. His parents are first cousins, and a younger sister has a similar rash and unexplained anemia. Angiographic findings are compatible with a medium-vessel vasculopathy.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this presentation?

options.B: Polyarteritis nodosa without an inherited immune disorder

item.tested_construct: DADA2 should be recognized in a child with livedo racemosa, systemic vasculitis/vasculopathy, hypertension, early lacunar strokes, hematologic abnormalities, and recessive familial clustering.

explanation.key_explanation: DADA2 is a recessive systemic autoinflammatory disorder that can mimic polyarteritis nodosa but is especially associated with childhood-onset vasculopathy, livedo, hypertension, ischemic or hemorrhagic strokes, immune dysregulation, and hematologic abnormalities.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. The early strokes, livedoid rash, medium-vessel disease, anemia, and consanguineous familial clustering are highly characteristic of DADA2.
distractor_explanations.B: Sporadic polyarteritis nodosa can produce medium-vessel vasculitis and livedo, but very early recurrent lacunar strokes plus an affected sibling and consanguinity strongly favor monogenic DADA2.
distractor_explanations.C: Antiphospholipid syndrome can cause thrombosis but does not explain this inherited childhood inflammatory vasculopathy with livedo and hematologic features.
distractor_explanations.D: Familial Mediterranean fever causes episodic fever and serositis but not this characteristic medium-vessel vasculopathy with childhood strokes.
distractor_explanations.E: Classic ADA-SCID causes profound combined immunodeficiency in infancy and lacks the characteristic cerebrocutaneous vasculitic phenotype of ADA2 deficiency.

explanation.educational_objective: Distinguish DADA2 from sporadic polyarteritis nodosa and other inflammatory disorders when childhood livedoid vasculopathy, hypertension, strokes, hematologic abnormalities, and recessive familial clustering occur together.

evidence_map.claim: Correct. The early strokes, livedoid rash, medium-vessel disease, anemia, and consanguineous familial clustering are highly characteristic of DADA2.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: PI3K-AKT-mTOR hyperactivation in activated PI3K-delta syndrome

item.vignette: A 12-year-old boy has recurrent otitis, sinusitis, and pneumonia, persistent lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and chronic Epstein-Barr virus viremia. Serum IgM is increased and IgG is decreased. Flow cytometry shows reduced naïve B and T lymphocytes. Sequencing identifies a heterozygous gain-of-function variant in PIK3CD, which encodes the p110δ catalytic subunit of phosphoinositide 3-kinase.
item.lead_in: Which intracellular signaling change is most directly caused by this variant?

options.A: Reduced JAK3-STAT5 signaling after common gamma-chain cytokine binding
options.B: Reduced BTK-dependent phospholipase C-gamma signaling downstream of the B-cell receptor
options.C: Failure of activation-induced cytidine deaminase activity during immunoglobulin class switching
options.E: Constitutive hyperactivation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway

item.tested_construct: PIK3CD gain-of-function in APDS1 causes hyperactivation of the PI3K-AKT-mTOR pathway, disrupting normal B- and T-cell maturation and function.

explanation.key_explanation: PIK3CD encodes p110δ, the leukocyte-enriched catalytic subunit of PI3K. Gain-of-function PIK3CD variants in APDS1 increase PI3K signaling, causing downstream AKT-mTOR hyperactivation and abnormal lymphocyte maturation/function.

distractor_explanations.A: JAK3-STAT5 failure is a severe combined immunodeficiency mechanism, not the downstream consequence of a gain-of-function PIK3CD variant.
distractor_explanations.B: BTK signaling failure causes X-linked agammaglobulinemia and is mechanistically distinct from PI3Kδ hyperactivation.
distractor_explanations.C: AID deficiency impairs class switching but does not explain the known signaling consequence of PIK3CD gain of function.
distractor_explanations.D: Reduced NF-kappaB activation is not the direct signaling effect of an activating p110δ mutation.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. APDS1 results from excessive PI3Kδ activity with hyperactivation of PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling.

explanation.educational_objective: Connect PIK3CD gain-of-function mutations in activated PI3K-delta syndrome to PI3K-AKT-mTOR hyperactivation and abnormal lymphocyte maturation.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Mechanistic link between C1q deficiency and lupus

item.vignette: A 7-year-old girl develops photosensitive facial rash, oral ulcers, arthritis, and glomerulonephritis. Antinuclear and anti-Smith antibodies are present. C1q is repeatedly undetectable, including during periods when her inflammatory symptoms are quiescent. Her parents are related.
item.lead_in: Loss of which normal immune function most directly contributes to this patient's autoimmune predisposition?

options.A: Assembly of the membrane attack complex for lysis of Neisseria species
options.B: Covalent C3b deposition as the principal opsonin for encapsulated bacteria
options.C: Recognition and clearance of apoptotic material that would otherwise provide persistent self-antigen
options.D: C5a-mediated chemotaxis and activation of neutrophils
options.E: Factor H-mediated restriction of alternative-pathway activation on host cells

item.tested_construct: Inherited C1q deficiency strongly predisposes to early SLE in part because impaired recognition/opsonization and clearance of apoptotic material increases exposure to self-antigens and loss of tolerance.

explanation.key_explanation: C1q is an early classical-pathway recognition molecule that binds apoptotic material and supports its noninflammatory clearance. Inherited C1q deficiency is strongly associated with early lupus; defective disposal of apoptotic debris permits prolonged exposure to nuclear self-antigens and promotes loss of tolerance.

distractor_explanations.A: Terminal complement components C5-C9 form the membrane attack complex; their deficiency classically predisposes to Neisseria infection rather than early lupus.
distractor_explanations.B: C3b is a major opsonin, but the question asks for the function whose loss links inherited C1q deficiency to autoimmunity.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. Impaired clearance of apoptotic material is a major mechanism linking early classical complement deficiency to lupus.
distractor_explanations.D: C5a is a downstream anaphylatoxin and neutrophil chemoattractant, not the principal autoimmune mechanism of C1q deficiency.
distractor_explanations.E: Factor H regulates the alternative pathway and is not the missing classical-pathway function in this patient.

explanation.educational_objective: Explain the paradox that deficiency of an early classical complement component can cause autoimmunity: failure to clear apoptotic material increases persistent self-antigen exposure and promotes loss of tolerance.

evidence_map.claim: Terminal complement components C5-C9 form the membrane attack complex; their deficiency classically predisposes to Neisseria infection rather than early lupus.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The complete vignette and named molecular/clinicopathologic features resolve this option under the single-best-answer lead-in.

item.vignette: A newborn is encased in a collodion membrane and later develops generalized plate-like scaling. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in PNPLA1. Electron microscopy shows an abnormal stratum-corneum lipid barrier.
item.lead_in: Which biochemical process is most directly impaired by this mutation?

options.A: Transfer of linoleic acid to omega-hydroxyceramide to generate omega-O-acylceramide
options.B: Hydrolysis of cholesterol sulfate in the outer epidermis
options.C: ATP-dependent delivery of glucosylceramides into lamellar granules
options.E: Proteolytic processing of profilaggrin into filaggrin-derived barrier components

item.tested_construct: PNPLA1 is a keratinocyte transacylase required for omega-O-acylceramide synthesis; loss impairs the stratum-corneum lipid barrier and causes autosomal-recessive congenital ichthyosis.

explanation.key_explanation: PNPLA1 transfers linoleate from triglycerides to omega-hydroxyceramides, producing omega-O-acylceramides that are essential components of the stratum-corneum lipid barrier. Loss of PNPLA1 therefore causes a primary acylceramide-synthesis defect.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. PNPLA1 catalyzes the linoleate-transfer step needed to form omega-O-acylceramides.
distractor_explanations.B: Steroid sulfatase deficiency causes X-linked ichthyosis by impaired cholesterol-sulfate hydrolysis, a different pathway.
distractor_explanations.C: ABCA12 transports lipids into lamellar granules; that is distinct from PNPLA1-catalyzed acylceramide synthesis.
distractor_explanations.D: TGM1 deficiency impairs cornified-envelope cross-linking and is another cause of autosomal-recessive congenital ichthyosis, but it is not PNPLA1's biochemical function.
distractor_explanations.E: Filaggrin processing contributes to barrier function but is not the direct reaction catalyzed by PNPLA1.

explanation.educational_objective: Link PNPLA1-associated congenital ichthyosis to failure of omega-O-acylceramide synthesis, specifically transfer of linoleate to omega-hydroxyceramide in differentiated keratinocytes.

evidence_map.claim: Correct. PNPLA1 catalyzes the linoleate-transfer step needed to form omega-O-acylceramides.

blueprint.coverage_deficit_addressed: Proteostasis mechanism of KLHL24-associated epidermolysis bullosa simplex

item.vignette: A newborn has large areas of denuded skin on the distal extremities and develops trauma-induced blistering. The blistering becomes less prominent with age, but skin atrophy persists. Several affected relatives later developed dilated cardiomyopathy. Sequencing identifies a heterozygous start-codon variant in KLHL24 that produces an N-terminally truncated protein.
item.lead_in: Which molecular consequence most directly causes the epidermal fragility?

options.A: Dominant-negative disruption of keratin 14 heterodimer assembly
options.B: Loss of type VII collagen anchoring fibrils beneath the lamina densa
options.C: Loss of collagen XVII-mediated attachment within hemidesmosomes
options.D: Failure to assemble laminin-332 in the basement membrane
options.E: Stabilization of a gain-of-function ubiquitin-ligase adaptor with excessive proteasomal degradation of keratin 14

item.tested_construct: KLHL24 start-codon variants stabilize a gain-of-function ubiquitin-ligase substrate adaptor, causing excessive ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of keratin 14 and an EBS phenotype that can include cardiomyopathy.

explanation.key_explanation: Disease-causing KLHL24 start-codon variants produce a truncated protein that is abnormally stable because normal autoubiquitination is lost. The stabilized gain-of-function protein excessively targets keratin 14 for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation, weakening basal keratinocytes.

distractor_explanations.A: Dominant-negative KRT14 variants can cause EBS, but the stem identifies a KLHL24 start-codon variant whose disease mechanism is abnormal proteasomal targeting of keratin.
distractor_explanations.B: COL7A1 defects cause dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa at the anchoring-fibril level, not this KLHL24-mediated intracellular keratin-degradation phenotype.
distractor_explanations.C: Collagen XVII defects affect hemidesmosomal adhesion but are not the molecular effect of an activating KLHL24 variant.
distractor_explanations.D: Laminin-332 deficiency causes junctional epidermolysis bullosa and does not explain the identified KLHL24 lesion.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. Stabilized mutant KLHL24 excessively ubiquitinates keratin 14, promoting its proteasomal degradation.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize a nonstructural cause of epidermolysis bullosa: KLHL24 gain of function increases ubiquitin-proteasome degradation of keratin 14 rather than directly mutating the keratin filament.

evidence_map.claim: Dominant-negative KRT14 variants can cause EBS, but the stem identifies a KLHL24 start-codon variant whose disease mechanism is abnormal proteasomal targeting of keratin.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The complete vignette and named molecular/clinicopathologic features resolve this option under the single-best-answer lead-in.

evidence_map.claim: COL7A1 defects cause dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa at the anchoring-fibril level, not this KLHL24-mediated intracellular keratin-degradation phenotype.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The complete vignette and named molecular/clinicopathologic features resolve this option under the single-best-answer lead-in.

evidence_map.claim: Collagen XVII defects affect hemidesmosomal adhesion but are not the molecular effect of an activating KLHL24 variant.

item.vignette: A 5-year-old boy born to consanguineous parents has lifelong trauma-induced skin erosions, painful palmoplantar thickening, sparse woolly hair, nail dystrophy, and reduced sweating. item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?

options.A: Kindler syndrome due to FERMT1 deficiency
options.B: Netherton syndrome due to SPINK5 deficiency
options.C: Ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility syndrome due to plakophilin 1 deficiency
options.D: Junctional epidermolysis bullosa due to laminin-332 deficiency

item.tested_construct: Biallelic PKP1 loss causes ectodermal dysplasia-skin fragility syndrome, characterized by trauma-induced erosions, hair/nail/sweat abnormalities, palmoplantar keratoderma, and poorly formed desmosomes with weak keratin attachment.

explanation.key_explanation: Plakophilin 1 is an accessory desmosomal plaque protein that helps couple the keratin cytoskeleton to desmosomal junctions. Biallelic PKP1 loss produces cutaneous fragility and ectodermal dysplasia, with structurally abnormal desmosomes and reduced keratin-filament attachment.

distractor_explanations.A: Kindler syndrome causes mixed-level skin fragility, photosensitivity, progressive poikiloderma, and mucosal disease rather than this desmosomal ectodermal-dysplasia phenotype.
distractor_explanations.B: Netherton syndrome is characterized by ichthyosis, severe atopy, and trichorrhexis invaginata due to SPINK5/LEKT1 deficiency, not poorly formed desmosomes from PKP1 loss.
distractor_explanations.C: Correct. The phenotype and desmosomal ultrastructure are characteristic of plakophilin 1 deficiency.
distractor_explanations.D: Laminin-332 deficiency causes junctional separation at the basement-membrane zone rather than widened intercellular spaces with malformed desmosomes.
distractor_explanations.E: Keratin 1/10 disorders cause epidermolytic hyperkeratosis and do not specifically produce this ectodermal-dysplasia/desmosomal phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize plakophilin 1 deficiency from trauma-induced skin fragility, ectodermal abnormalities, palmoplantar keratoderma, and malformed desmosomes with poor keratin-filament attachment.

item.vignette: A 10-month-old girl has had generalized superficial skin peeling and erythema since the neonatal period. She has severe pruritus, food allergies, and elevated serum IgE. Hair microscopy is normal, and immunostaining shows normal LEKT1 expression. Her parents are first cousins.

options.D: Generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome due to corneodesmosin deficiency

item.tested_construct: Autosomal-recessive CDSN loss causes generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome with superficial peeling, pruritus, atopy, and epidermal-barrier failure; normal LEKT1 and hair findings help exclude Netherton syndrome.

explanation.key_explanation: Corneodesmosin is an adhesion component in the upper epidermis. Biallelic CDSN loss causes generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome, characterized by lifelong superficial peeling, erythema/pruritus, barrier dysfunction, and marked atopy. Normal LEKT1 and hair microscopy argue against Netherton syndrome.

distractor_explanations.A: Netherton syndrome can cause erythroderma and atopy, but normal LEKT1 expression and normal hair microscopy make it less likely.
distractor_explanations.B: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome is an acute toxin-mediated illness rather than a lifelong recessive peeling disorder with atopy.
distractor_explanations.C: Ichthyosis vulgaris causes dry scaling and is associated with filaggrin deficiency; continuous inflammatory superficial peeling is not its typical phenotype.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. CDSN deficiency causes generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome through impaired upper-epidermal adhesion and barrier failure.
distractor_explanations.E: Acral peeling skin syndrome is predominantly localized to hands and feet, unlike this generalized inflammatory phenotype.

explanation.educational_objective: Differentiate CDSN-related generalized inflammatory peeling skin syndrome from Netherton and other peeling/ichthyotic disorders by lifelong generalized superficial peeling, severe atopy, normal LEKT1, and normal hair microscopy.

item.vignette: An 11-year-old boy born to consanguineous parents has had generalized trauma-induced blistering and nail dystrophy since infancy. Over the past 2 years, he has developed progressive proximal muscle weakness, and serum creatine kinase is elevated. Electron microscopy of a skin biopsy shows cleavage within basal keratinocytes just above the hemidesmosomes.
item.lead_in: Which diagnosis best explains this combination of findings?

options.A: Duchenne muscular dystrophy with an unrelated blistering disorder
options.B: PLEC-associated epidermolysis bullosa simplex with muscular dystrophy
options.D: Integrin alpha6-beta4-associated junctional epidermolysis bullosa with pyloric atresia

item.tested_construct: Biallelic PLEC variants cause epidermolysis bullosa simplex with muscular dystrophy because plectin mechanically couples intermediate-filament networks in basal keratinocytes and muscle.

explanation.key_explanation: Plectin is a cytoskeletal linker expressed in skin and muscle. Biallelic PLEC variants can cause EBS with generalized blistering followed by progressive muscular dystrophy. The cleavage plane within basal keratinocytes just above hemidesmosomes supports an EBS-level defect.

distractor_explanations.A: A single pleiotropic cytoskeletal disorder explains both skin and muscle findings, making two unrelated disorders unnecessary.
distractor_explanations.B: Correct. PLEC-associated EBS with muscular dystrophy unifies basal-keratinocyte fragility and progressive myopathy.
distractor_explanations.C: COL7A1 defects cause dystrophic EB with cleavage below the lamina densa at anchoring fibrils and do not characteristically cause this PLEC-associated myopathy.
distractor_explanations.D: Integrin alpha6-beta4 disease is a junctional EB phenotype often associated with pyloric atresia; the cleavage plane and later muscular dystrophy instead support PLEC-associated EBS.
distractor_explanations.E: Desmoplakin disorders can affect skin and heart, but basal-cell cleavage above hemidesmosomes plus progressive muscular dystrophy is characteristic of PLEC-associated EBS.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize PLEC-associated EBS with muscular dystrophy when lifelong basal-keratinocyte skin fragility is followed by progressive myopathy, reflecting plectin's role as an intermediate-filament cytoskeletal linker in both tissues.

evidence_map.claim: A single pleiotropic cytoskeletal disorder explains both skin and muscle findings, making two unrelated disorders unnecessary.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The complete vignette and named molecular/clinicopathologic features resolve this option under the single-best-answer lead-in.
